summary: Band: a 14th-century Byzantine fresco of Polycarp, head and shoulders, face large and clear (the lead picture of the English and Russian Wikipedia articles). Second picture from the other half of the Church: F. E. Ring's 1884 statue on Frederik's Church (the Marble Church), Copenhagen, a Lutheran church. Gallery: Jan Luyken's 1701 etching of the flames arching round him (the miracle of Martyrdom chapter 15, with the dagger of chapter 16), the 6th-century Ravenna procession of martyrs, an anonymous engraved portrait in profile (Wellcome Collection, Public Domain Mark: see its note), and Michael Burghers's engraving for William Cave's Apostolici. Only ONE Luyken print is used. Card: cropped from the band fresco.

pictures.title: Saint Polycarp (ὁ ἅγιος Πολύκαρπος), fresco
pictures.artist: Workshop of Michael Astrapas and Eutychios (the painters of St George's, Staro Nagoričane)
pictures.collection: Church of St George, Staro Nagoričane, North Macedonia (in situ)

faceBox.note: hair top to mouth; the beard runs on down to about 54% of the height. Suggested object-position: phone 50% 14%, wide 50% 16%.

pictures.alt: A Byzantine fresco: Saint Polycarp, an old bishop with a high bald forehead, tired dark eyes and a long white beard, before an orange halo on a deep blue wall, his white vestment marked with large dark red crosses, his name in Greek letters beside his head
pictures.credit: Saint Polycarp, fresco, Church of St George, Staro Nagoričane, North Macedonia, about 1317. Public domain.
pictures.note: Chosen over every alternative because the face is large, frontal and crisp: it carries a 390x335 phone band and a 46%-wide, 26rem panel with room to spare. Long side 1182 px (the largest copy that exists of this fresco on Commons; nothing larger found). LICENCE: the tag is CC0, but the uploader's 'own work' claim cannot be checked (the photo looks like a scan of a printed reproduction). It does not matter for the site: the painting is 700 years old and on a flat wall panel, so any faithful photo of it is public domain under the same rule (PD-Art) that covers the other Byzantine frescoes on the hub. That is why the credit says 'Public domain', not 'CC0'. LOCATION: the English Wikipedia caption and the Commons category say Staro Nagoričane; a second upload of the SAME fresco (File:Polycarp_of_Smyrna_fresco.jpg, 2024) describes it as St Nicholas Orphanos, Thessaloniki, 14th century. I could not settle it from a church source (the Staro Nagoričane wall photos on Commons do not show this panel). Both churches were painted about 1310-1320 by painters of the same Thessaloniki circle. If the writer wants no risk, use: 'Saint Polycarp, a Byzantine fresco of the early 1300s, probably Staro Nagoričane, North Macedonia. Public domain.'

pictures.role: portrait (second picture, the Western half: a Lutheran church)
pictures.title: Polykarp, statue on the exterior of Frederik's Church (the Marble Church)
pictures.licenceTag: {{PD-self}} (photo by Orf3us, 2010); the sculptor died in 1886, so the statue itself is public domain

faceBox.note: face looks up and to the left; beard included. Suggested object-position 50% 18%.

pictures.alt: A pale stone statue of Polycarp as an old bearded man in a heavy draped cloak, arms held out low with open hands, face lifted toward the sky, against the grey stone and a dark window of a church wall
pictures.credit: Saint Polycarp, statue by Ferdinand Edvard Ring, 1884. Frederik's Church (the Marble Church), Copenhagen. Photo: Orf3us, public domain.
pictures.caption: Ferdinand Edvard Ring's statue of 1884 stands on the outside of Copenhagen's Marble Church, a Lutheran church, among the great teachers of the Church. Public domain.
pictures.note: A photo of a 3D object, so it needed PD-self or CC0: it is PD-self. Good for the 'both halves' pairing: an Eastern fresco in the band, a Western (Lutheran) statue beside the facts. Colour photo, stone in soft daylight. The caption's 'among the great teachers of the Church' is a description, not a sourced claim about the programme of statues: drop it if the writer cannot check it; the rest is on the Commons page.

pictures.title: H. Polycarpus wordt op een brandstapel gezet maar de vlammen verbranden hem niet (Saint Polycarp is set on a pyre but the flames do not burn him)
pictures.date: 1701 (proof of an illustration for the Dutch edition of Gottfried Arnold's Wahre Abbildung der ersten Christen, Amsterdam, 1700, volume 2)

faceBox.note: a scene: Polycarp is the small seated figure inside the ring of fire, upper centre; do not crop to a face

pictures.alt: An etching: a great ring of flame billows up like a sail round Polycarp, who sits unharmed on the pyre inside it, while a crowd, soldiers and a magistrate on a temple porch look on and a man in the foreground throws up his arms in wonder
pictures.credit: Saint Polycarp in the flames, Jan Luyken, 1701. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. CC0.
pictures.caption: Jan Luyken draws what the Martyrdom says the watchers saw: the fire made "the shape of a vault" round him. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. CC0.
pictures.note: Exactly the scene of Martyrdom of Polycarp chapters 15 and 16: the fire forms an arch like a ship's sail round him, and at the right an executioner comes forward with a blade. The only Luyken on the page: his 1698 Fathers series print of Polycarp (RP-P-1896-A-19368-1256) and his 1685 Martyrs Mirror etching were left out to avoid the repetition the owner may dislike. The caption quotes nothing yet; the writer must fit any quoted words to the checked Lightfoot or Lake text of chapter 15. Saved as greyscale (the print is black and white) to keep it under 450 KB at 1500 px.

pictures.role: gallery 2 (the oldest kind of picture: a 6th-century mosaic)
pictures.title: Procession of the Holy Martyrs (detail: SCS POLICARPVS, beside Saint Vincent)
pictures.date: about 560 (the martyrs' procession belongs to the redecoration under Bishop Agnellus after 561; Commons says 'before 526', which is the date of Theodoric's first mosaics, not of this frieze)
pictures.collection: Basilica of Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, Ravenna, Italy

faceBox.note: Polycarp is the bearded, grey-haired martyr on the left, under the letters POLICARPVS

pictures.alt: A mosaic on gold: two haloed martyrs in white robes walk in procession carrying jewelled crowns, the older one on the left grey-haired and bearded, with his Latin name in the band of letters above
pictures.credit: Saint Polycarp in the procession of martyrs, mosaic, Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, Ravenna, about 560. Photo: Sibeaster, public domain.
pictures.caption: In the 500s Ravenna set him in a long procession of martyrs carrying their crowns to Christ. Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, Ravenna. Public domain.
pictures.note: Cropped from a 1632x1224 photo of the whole frieze, lightly brightened and de-noised; only 640x740, so it suits the gallery (wide screens, small) but never the band. A sharper, larger photo exists (File:Meister_von_San_Apollinare_Nuovo_in_Ravenna_001.jpg, Yorck Project, 2048x1338, from which File:St_Polycarp-ApollinareNuovoRavenna.JPG is cut) but it is tagged PD-Art-YorckProject: a photo of a mosaic is a 3D object under the hub's rule, so it was not used. The site may drop this picture if it looks too dark or soft beside the others.

pictures.title: Saint Polycarp. Engraving. (lettered S. POLYCARPUS)
pictures.date: undated (no date in the Wellcome record; do not print one)
pictures.collection: Wellcome Collection, London, Wellcome Library no. 6883i, image V0032929
pictures.licenceTag: Commons tag: {{CC-BY-4.0}} (Wellcome's licence at the 2014 upload). Wellcome Collection's own record TODAY: Public Domain Mark (https://creativecommons.org/share-your-work/public-domain/pdm/), read from its catalogue API on 2026-09-25.

faceBox.note: profile facing right; hair and head from about left 27%

pictures.alt: An engraving in a ruled frame: Saint Polycarp in profile facing right, an old man with a bald crown, long hair and a long flowing beard, a halo behind his head, lettered S. POLYCARPUS below, with a tiny scene of a man and a lion in the top corner
pictures.credit: S. Polycarpus, an anonymous engraving. Wellcome Collection, London. Public domain.
pictures.caption: An engraved portrait, maker and date unknown. The little scene in the corner shows a lion, which the crowd called for but never got. Wellcome Collection, London. Public domain.
pictures.note: The strongest face after the band, but READ THE LICENCE NOTE: the Commons page still carries CC BY 4.0, while the holder, Wellcome Collection, now marks it Public Domain Mark. If the rule 'the Commons tag decides' is applied strictly, drop this picture (Burghers, below, is a clean fallback) or credit it from the Wellcome page with its Public Domain Mark. Faint show-through of English printed text from the back of the leaf is visible in the background. The corner scene of a lion is odd for Polycarp (no lion was set on him): the caption above ties it to Martyrdom chapter 12, where the crowd asked Philip the Asiarch to loose a lion on him and he refused; the writer should check that wording against the text or cut the sentence.

pictures.role: gallery 4 (engraved full figure, with Smyrna behind)
pictures.title: S. Polycarpus (plate in William Cave, Apostolici: or, the history of the lives, acts, death, and martyrdoms of those who were contemporary with, or immediately succeeded the Apostles, London, 1716 edition, page 121)
pictures.artist: Michael Burghers (signed 'Michael Burghers delineavit et sculpsit')
pictures.date: the book first appeared in 1677; this impression is from the 1716 edition
pictures.collection: Cambridge University Library copy, via the Fleuron database (https://fleuron.lib.cam.ac.uk/ornament/038910010001210_0)

faceBox.note: full-length figure; face near the top of the oval

pictures.alt: An engraving in an oval frame: Polycarp stands full length in a long cloak, bearded, holding a book and raising one hand, with a walled harbour town and hills behind him, lettered S. POLYCARPUS below
pictures.credit: S. Polycarpus, Michael Burghers, from William Cave's Apostolici, London, 1716 edition. Public domain.
pictures.caption: Michael Burghers engraved him for William Cave's lives of the first Fathers, with a harbour town behind him that stands for Smyrna. Public domain.
pictures.note: The scan is a black-and-white threshold (hard, grainy lines); smoothed very slightly and saved greyscale. Its left edge is cut into the frame in the source scan itself. That the town is Smyrna is my reading of the picture (a port with shipping), not a label: soften to 'a harbour town' if unsure. The small 300 px copy on Commons (File:Burghers_michael_saintpolycarp.jpg, used by Wikipedia with 'c. 1685') is the same plate.
